challenges.title: Spawn and Execute External Command
challenges.description: Your shell needs to be able to invoke system binaries like 'ls', 'echo', or 'cat' by passing the appropriate arguments.
challenges.task: Implement a Function executeCommand that takes a command name and a slice of string arguments, creates an exec.Cmd object, connects its standard output and error to the console, and starts it.
hints: Use the exec.Command function from the os/exec package.
Assign os.Stdout and os.Stderr to your Cmd struct fields.
Call the Run() method on your command object to execute it.

challenges.title: Wait for Process Completion
challenges.description: Understanding separate start and wait phases is crucial for implementing background jobs and foreground synchronization in your shell.
challenges.task: Implement a Function runAndWait that uses Cmd.Start() to launch a background process and then explicitly calls Cmd.Wait() to wait for its completion and return any error.
hints: Call cmd.Start() and handle any startup error.
Call cmd.Wait() to block until the process exits.

challenges.title: Graceful Error Handling for Missing Binaries
challenges.description: Users will often make typos or type commands that are not installed. Your shell must gracefully report these failures.
challenges.task: Write a function safeExecute that wraps command execution and checks if the returned error matches exec.ErrNotFound or other execution failures, printing a friendly error message instead of panicking.
hints: Inspect the error returned by Cmd.Run().
Use errors.Is(err, exec.ErrNotFound) to check for missing executables.
